Middle East.headline: Gaza Health Officials Report Four Killed in Israeli Strikes Amid Ongoing Offensive
Middle East.body: Health officials in the Gaza Strip reported on Saturday that at least four Palestinians, including a 10-year-old child and the son of a senior government official, were killed in a series of Israeli military strikes across the enclave. The casualties occurred despite an ongoing, albeit fragile, ceasefire framework that was brokered by the United States late last year, highlighting the persistent volatility and lethal risks that continue to define the daily reality for civilians in the territory. Middle East.headline: At least 80 Houthis killed as Yemen army repels fierce attacks on Marib
Middle East.body: Yemeni government forces repelled fierce Houthi attacks outside Marib, killing at least 80 fighters and destroying nine military vehicles in 24 hours of intense combat. The clashes erupted in areas south of the strategically important city, including Hareb, Mala'a and Um Raish, as Iran-backed forces intensified their push to seize the energy-rich province. Brigadier General Yahya Al-Hatemi, director of the Yemeni army's military media department, confirmed that government troops, backed by warplanes and drones, forced Houthi fighters to retreat from their positions. Americas.headline: More than a dozen arrested in connection with 2021 assassination of Haitian president
Americas.body: Jovenel Moïse, 53, was shot dead in July 2021 in a killing which sparked chaos in Haiti Eighteen people have been arrested in association with the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, according to US officials. Moïse, 53, was shot dead on 7 July 2021 at his private residence by a hired group of about 20 military-trained Colombian mercenaries. His security detail did not intervene to protect him. Americas.headline: UAE sends aid to Colombia under $10 million earthquake relief campaign
Americas.body: The UAE on Sunday delivered critical aid to Colombia under a $10 million relief package set up last month in response to a powerful earthquake which killed more than 300 people and injured thousands more. The essential supplies flown into the South American country - including food, hygiene kits and cleaning equipment - will support communities still reeling from the natural disaster. The 7.4-magnitude quake struck near the town of San Jose del Palmar in Choco province on August 10, with its impact felt across large parts of western Colombia. Africa.body: Sudan is hurtling toward a catastrophic man-made famine engineered deliberately by warring military factions, a regional human rights organisation has warned, as collapsing agricultural conditions and blocked aid routes compound the suffering of millions. Africa.headline: Ebola death toll rises to 3,699 in DR Congo as response continues
Africa.body: The toll from an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has climbed to 3,699 as health authorities work to contain the disease, which is spreading rapidly. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, has spread to several provinces and Ituri remains the main epicentre. As part of efforts to strengthen the response, the Congo started vaccinating frontline health workers in Ituri on Saturday. The vaccination campaign is employing the Ervebo vaccine, approved for a different strain of Ebola virus, under a compassionate-use programme. Europe.headline: Moscow: Ukraine launches huge drone attack as election wraps up
Europe.body: Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds at the capital Moscow, in its largest attack of the war so far, officials said Sunday. The attack came as Russia wrapped up the final day of voting in tightly controlled parliamentary elections that President Vladimir Putin has cast as a test of support for the war in Ukraine.

Europe.headline: Putin party retains majority in first vote since 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Europe.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party won a large majority in parliamentary elections, according to preliminary results published by state media Monday, in a vote held amid Ukrainian drone strikes, cyberattacks and a crackdown on anti-war opposition. The election was the first since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. France 24 International affairs editor, Oliver Farry, shares further insights from this election.

Europe.headline: Russia: Kremlin party dominates controlled vote
Europe.body: In Russia, early results from the parliamentary election show the Kremlin-backed United Russia party leading in the tightly controlled vote. The election, the country’s first parliamentary ballot held during wartime, began on Friday and concluded on Sunday, with around 111 million people eligible to vote. Moscow’s mayor said voting went ahead as planned despite Ukrainian drone attacks. Charlotte Hughes reports.

Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship.
